metadata.title: Example Fleet Readiness Analytics Service Security Assessment Report (draft)

results.title: Control assessment results
results.description: Results of assessing the controls of baseline CNSSI1253-M-M-L-SUBSET-50 per the assessment plan.

reviewed-controls.description: The controls of baseline CNSSI1253-M-M-L-SUBSET-50 in the assessment scope.

observations.title: ac-1 determination
observations.description: Examined the access control chapter of the EFRAS security operations runbook (version 2.1, re-issued by the ISSM 2026-06-15, previous annual review 2025-10-20), its repository access list (the six engineers, four app-admins and the ISSO) and its reference to the Component access control policy; interviewed the ISSO. The organization-level policy is the Component's (ART-ORG-CONTEXT); its own annual review is the Component's and is accepted on its issue date.

observations.title: ac-2 determination
observations.description: Examined access requests and approvals for a random sample across the five roles, the 2026-10-06 quarterly review record, the 35-day inactivity setting and the role-change events; re-ran six DT-2 sign-in and inactivity cases (pass); interviewed the ISSO. Account types, approvals, provisioning through broker groups, monitoring and the quarterly review are in place. The leaver-timing test (PRC-004, 2026-12-01) of ten leavers found no evidence that any departure reached the account manager within the 24 hours the SSP sets: the two known leavers were removed only at the quarterly review, and the other eight checklists record no notification time (ASM-020). Account management is not aligned with the termination and transfer processes. Pre-production accounts only.

observations.title: ac-3 determination
observations.description: Examined the API authorization middleware, the report service's scope check added in release 1.5.1 and the sandbox workload's grants; tested 100 crafted cross-squadron and cross-air-wing requests across the five roles through the UI, the API and the PT-1 export path (all refused) and reused the red team result (RR-002) with the PT-1 retest pass of 2026-11-10; interviewed the developer. Approved authorizations are enforced on every path tested, in pre-production.

observations.title: ac-6 determination
observations.description: Examined every privileged role (4 app-admins, 6 named console roles, the break-glass console and database accounts) against the 2026-10-06 review and the duty lists, and the nine workload identities' namespace bindings; tested the four privileged roles and confirmed a viewer and an analyst cannot change roles or reach the sandbox; interviewed the developer. Privileges match the duties; no cluster-wide workload grant was found.

observations.title: ac-17 determination
observations.description: Examined the runbook's remote access section (two access types with usage restrictions, connection requirements and guidance) and the ISSM's authorization memo of 2026-03-10; tested that the edge accepts only 443 with TLS 1.2 or 1.3 after CAC sign-in and that the cluster API has no public endpoint; interviewed the ISSO.

observations.title: at-2 determination
observations.description: Examined the Component training system and privacy office completion reports for 30 accounts drawn from the 141 (all current, initial completion before account creation), the October and November lapsed-training lists (no EFRAS user), the sign-in banner, the 1.5.0 and 1.5.1 release-note notices, the quarterly reminders of 2026-07-01 and 2026-10-01, and the privacy training revisions of 2026-04-01 and 2026-06-10 (after a Component breach); interviewed the ISSM and the privacy officer. The privacy office's part was examined as delivered to EFRAS users.

observations.title: at-3 determination
observations.description: Examined the privileged user training report and the runbook walk-through attendance list against the privileged account list (six engineers, four app-admins, three data scientists, the ISSO): each completion predates the privilege grant and is within the year; the walk-through was updated for release 1.5 on 2026-06-15 and the privileged course carries a privacy module; interviewed the ISSM and the privacy officer.

observations.title: au-2 determination
observations.description: Examined the runbook event list with its per-event rationale, the CSSP onboarding ticket of 2026-04-22 that set the use cases and the 2026-06-15 review; triggered the eight auditable event types the SSP lists (request and WAF hit, sign-in, role change, export, admin action, failed authorization, cluster API call, database login) and traced each to CMP-LOGS and the CSSP within five minutes, re-performing the DT-2 export audit case; interviewed the ISSO. STG-001 (database connection logging verbosity) is assessed under cm-6, where I-2 mapped it; the database login events the SSP lists were recorded.

observations.title: au-6 determination
observations.description: Examined 13 weekly review reports (2026-08-17 to 2026-11-09), the daily reports of the raised-threat week in 2026-09, the pager history and three CSSP tickets with their dispositions; tested that a break-glass sign-in and an export volume spike page the on-call engineer and open a CSSP ticket; interviewed the ISSO and the CSSP liaison. The CSSP's 24x7 correlation was observed through its ingestion dashboard, not re-assessed (EXT-004).

observations.title: au-9 determination
observations.description: Examined the log store's 90-day write-once lock, its read policy (ISSO and auditor roles only, no delete) and the policy-change alert history; tested a delete and a policy change with an engineer's role (both refused, the attempt alerted the ISSO and the ISSM); interviewed the ISSO.

observations.title: au-11 determination
observations.description: Examined the retention settings of the three log stores and queried each for its oldest record: each holds 90 days, against the one-year retention the tailored control sets. The CSSP's one-year copy is kept under the CSSP's own schedule, retrievable only by ticket and changeable without the program's agreement, so it does not meet the program's retention duty. Interviewed the ISSO and the CSSP liaison. The SSP records the control as partial, with an archive tier in release 1.6.

observations.title: ca-2 determination
observations.description: Examined sap.yaml and ART-SAP: the AODR selected an independent team on 2026-11-18 and approved the plan, which names the 50 controls, 17 procedures, the pre-production environment, the team and the roles, on 2026-11-18, before the assessment started on 2026-11-19. Interviewed the ISSM. This assessment is the first; no assessment report has yet been produced or delivered, and the recurring annual assessment of a third of the controls is written into ART-CONMON but not yet scheduled. The SSP statement for ca-2 predates A-1 and A-2 and still says no assessor is selected (left to A-5).

observations.title: ca-3 determination
observations.description: Examined the supply status service agreement (2026-06-30) and the identity broker onboarding approval (2026-05-12), both signed and documenting interface, security and privacy requirements, responsibilities and impact level; examined the EMIS ISSM's interim e-mail approval of 2026-09-15, which names only the interface; tested the EFRAS end of each exchange (mutual TLS and signature check on the EMIS extract, read-only API pull, SAML assertion validation), all as designed. Interviewed the PM. The EMIS exchange, which carries maintainer PII, is not approved and managed by an agreement: the memorandum of agreement is unsigned (target 2026-12-31).

observations.title: ca-5 determination
observations.description: Examined the eMASS POA&M module (empty) and the program backlog tickets for the seven known limitations; interviewed the ISSM and the PM. No plan of action and milestones exists yet; the known weaknesses are tracked only as backlog tickets with fix releases. The SSP records ca-5 as planned, to be met at A-6.

observations.title: ca-7 determination
observations.description: Examined ART-CONMON, approved by the AODR on 2026-11-18 with its metrics and frequencies, and the pre-production monitoring records: weekly scans and log reviews, hourly drift reports, the 2026-10-06 account review, the CSSP's correlation tickets and the backlog tickets they raised. Interviewed the ISSM and the PM. No ongoing control assessment has run and no security or privacy status report (monthly roll-up, quarterly posture report) has been produced under the strategy; the SSP records ca-7 as planned until the first cycle after authorization.

observations.title: cm-2 determination
observations.description: Examined the version-controlled templates and the 1.5.0 and 1.5.1 manifests of image digests (both releases updated them) and 90 days of hourly drift reports (one manual node label change, reverted the same day); compared 20 deployed resources on CMP-K8S and CMP-DB with the baseline (all matched); reused RR-001 for the node and database settings; interviewed the ISSE. The deployed state assessed is pre-production, built from the same templates as production (F-11-9).

observations.title: cm-3 determination
observations.description: Examined a random sample of 8 of the 23 pull requests merged between releases 1.5.0 and 1.5.1 (each with a second reviewer, a security and privacy impact note, green gates and an ISSE or ISSO sign-off; no emergency change), the CCB minutes of 2026-09 to 2026-11, and the retention of repository and pipeline records; tested that a direct change to the cluster outside the pipeline is reported by the drift scan within the hour; interviewed the ISSE.

observations.title: cm-6 determination
observations.description: Reused RR-001 and ran the SCA's authenticated scan of release 1.5.1 on 2026-11-23 over the nodes, the images and the database instance: same result as 2026-10-22, nodes 94% with only provider-managed control plane checks open, database with STG-001 and STG-002 open (program-fixable, release 1.5.2 not yet in pre-production) and STG-003 to STG-006 recorded as the provider's settings under LA-01; no CAT I. Examined ART-STIG and stig-summary.yaml, the drift reports and the change records. The Application Security and Development STIG review of INV-002 to INV-006 (BM-04, 2026-11-24) found no documented secure configuration for the five containers to review against (ASM-021). Interviewed the ISSE and the developer.

observations.title: cm-8 determination
observations.description: Compared 20 deployed resources (nodes, images, database, buckets, keys) with the INV list: every one is listed, none twice, none belonging to another system, with the fields the SSP names. The inventory still records the five containers at 1.5.0 while release 1.5.1 has run in the assessed environment since 2026-11-07, and no review at that release is recorded, although the SSP sets review at every release. Interviewed the ISSE.

observations.title: cp-2 determination
observations.description: Examined the whole of the contingency plan, version 1.0 draft (ART-CP), against the control: it covers the essential function, the 24-hour objectives, restoration order and metrics, roles with the on-call roster, continued reporting from EMIS during an outage, restoration from the templates, coordination with incident handling through the CSSP ticket path, and repository protection. It has not been reviewed or approved by the PM, has not been distributed to the key personnel or to EMIS and the CSSP, has had no annual review, and no change to it has been communicated. Interviewed the ISSE. The SSP records cp-2 as partial; the S-6 approval asks the PM to approve it by 2026-12-15.

observations.title: cp-4 determination
observations.description: Examined the plan and every test record: the only test is the DT-2 database point-in-time restore (3 h 10 min). Re-performed that restore on 2026-12-02 in pre-production: it finished well inside the 24-hour objective and the ISSE reviewed the result; no corrective action was needed. No regional failover of the cluster and no tabletop exercise has been held (planned 2027-02), so the plan's effectiveness and the readiness to execute it are not tested as the tailored control sets (annual tabletop, restore and failover tests). Interviewed the ISSE.

observations.title: cp-9 determination
observations.description: Examined point-in-time recovery and daily snapshots on CMP-DB encrypted with program-owned keys, versioning and deletion protection on the CMP-OBJ buckets, and version control for templates, manifests and documents; the restore re-performed under cp-4 shows the backups usable. The provider's snapshot and durability part was confirmed against its package and October deliverable (EXT-001), not re-tested. Interviewed the ISSE and the provider's liaison.

observations.title: ia-2 determination
observations.description: Tested CAC sign-in through the broker for all five roles and the six console roles (re-performing DT-2), and traced the DoD ID number from the assertion to the session and to every audit event of the test (uniquely tied); refused a sign-in without an approved group. Examined the two break-glass console accounts: they authenticate with FIDO2 keys, not CAC, and a use is tied to a person only by the two-person seal log and the alert; neither has been used. The deviation from the DoD CAC requirement has not been put to the AO. Interviewed the ISSO. The SSP records ia-2 as partial for this reason.

observations.title: ia-5 determination
observations.description: Examined the FIDO2 key issue record (in person against ID, defaults changed at issue), the key service inventory (no long-lived access keys; program keys rotated 2026-03-02), the break-glass database password change record (2026-07-01, inside 180 days) and the seal log; tested that a workload token expires with its session. The local break-glass database role's password complexity falls short of the PostgreSQL STIG rule on both the 2026-10-22 scan and the SCA's 2026-11-23 scan (STG-002, CAT II, fix in release 1.5.2). Interviewed the ISSO.

findings.title: Departures do not reach the account manager within 24 hours; leaver accounts stay active until the quarterly review
findings.description: AC-2 as tailored requires account managers to be notified within 24 hours when users are terminated or transferred, accounts to be disabled per that policy, and account management aligned with termination and transfer. The 2026-10-06 review found two accounts of users who had left a pilot squadron still active; they were removed at the review, not on departure. The leaver-timing test of ten leavers (2026-12-01) found no notification time for any of them: the out-processing step relies on an e-mail from the squadron office that was not sent for the two known leavers and is not recorded for the others. Evidence: the account review record, the ISSO interview, the out-processing checklists (ASM-020).
findings.remarks: Feed departures and transfers from the squadrons' out-processing into the account manager's queue automatically (or a recorded hand-off with a timestamp), disable the EFRAS account and remove the broker group within 24 hours, and check leaver timing in each quarterly review until production.

findings.title: Audit records are retained 90 days, not the one year the tailored control requires
findings.description: AU-11 as tailored requires audit records retained for one year to support after-the-fact investigations and Component retention requirements. The three log stores hold 90 days; the oldest record each returned on query was 90 days old. The CSSP keeps a one-year copy for its own analysis, retrievable by ticket and under a schedule the program does not control. Evidence: log store retention settings and lifecycle rules, the retrieval test, the ISSO and CSSP interviews, the known limitation (conops item 6).
findings.remarks: Add the archive tier (release 1.6) holding one year of records under the program's control; until then record in the CSSP agreement that the CSSP keeps EFRAS records one year and returns them on request within a set time.

findings.title: No control assessment has yet been completed and reported, and the recurring assessment is not scheduled
findings.description: CA-2 requires controls to be assessed annually (a third each year), an assessment report produced and the results provided to the AO, the PM and the ISSM. The assessor selection and the approved plan are in place (2026-11-18). This first assessment is in progress; no report has yet been produced or delivered, and the annual assessment set is not chosen or scheduled. Evidence: sap.yaml, ART-SAP, ART-CONMON, the ISSM interview.
findings.remarks: Deliver this assessment's report (A-4) to the AO, the PM and the ISSM, then choose and schedule the first annual third of the controls in the continuous monitoring plan, and update the ca-2 SSP statement to the as-assessed state.

findings.title: The EMIS exchange runs on an interim e-mail approval with no signed agreement
findings.description: CA-3 requires each information exchange to be approved and managed through an agreement documenting interface characteristics, security and privacy requirements, controls, responsibilities and the impact level. The nightly EMIS extract, which carries maintainer PII and CUI, runs on the EMIS ISSM's interim e-mail approval of 2026-09-15, which names only the interface; the memorandum of agreement is drafted and under legal review (target 2026-12-31). The two other exchanges have signed agreements. The EFRAS end's mutual TLS and signature check were tested and work. Evidence: the agreements, the interim e-mail, the PM interview, conops limitation 3.
findings.remarks: Sign the EFRAS-EMIS memorandum of agreement with the security and privacy requirements, breach notification, responsibilities of each side and the impact level, before production data flows; record it in boundary.yaml and the SSP.

findings.title: No plan of action and milestones exists for the system
findings.description: CA-5 requires a POA&M documenting planned remediation of weaknesses and known vulnerabilities, updated monthly. The eMASS POA&M module is empty; the seven known limitations are tracked only as backlog tickets with fix releases. Evidence: eMASS, the backlog, the ISSM and PM interviews.
findings.remarks: Create the POA&M at A-6 from this assessment's findings, the open STIG items and the known limitations, with milestones and dates, and update it monthly.

findings.title: Continuous monitoring has not yet run under the approved strategy: no ongoing assessment and no status reporting
findings.description: CA-7 requires system-level continuous monitoring under the strategy, including ongoing control assessments and reporting of the security and privacy status to the AO through the AODR, the PM and the ISSM. The strategy was approved on 2026-11-18 and scanning, log review, drift checks and account reviews run in pre-production, but no ongoing control assessment has run and neither the monthly roll-up nor the quarterly posture report has been produced. Evidence: ART-CONMON, the monitoring records, the ISSM and PM interviews.
findings.remarks: Run the first monitoring cycle after the decision as ART-CONMON sets out, produce the first monthly roll-up and quarterly posture report, and start the annual third of control assessments.

findings.title: Database connection logging verbosity is below the PostgreSQL STIG value (STG-001, CAT II)
findings.description: CM-6 requires the established configuration settings to be implemented. The SCA-witnessed scan of 2026-10-22 and the SCA's scan of release 1.5.1 on 2026-11-23 both show the connection logging verbosity on INV-010 below the PostgreSQL STIG value (STG-001, CAT II). The fix is in release 1.5.2 (2026-12-10), which had not reached pre-production by the scan. Evidence: RR-001, the 2026-11-23 scan, stig-summary.yaml, the ISSE and developer interviews.
findings.remarks: Deploy release 1.5.2 with the corrected setting, rescan the database and close STG-001 on the scan result.

findings.title: No secure configuration is established for the five application containers (Application Security and Development STIG not applied)
findings.description: CM-6 requires configuration settings reflecting the most restrictive mode consistent with operations to be established and documented for the components, using the common secure configurations the SSP names. The five application containers (INV-002 to INV-006), which hold and serve the PII and CUI, have no documented settings against the Application Security and Development STIG; the program never completed the checklist (ASM-019), and the assessor's review on 2026-11-24 had nothing to compare the containers against (ASM-021). The pipeline scans and the factory base image cover vulnerabilities and the base layer, not the application settings. Evidence: stig-summary.yaml BM-04, the developer and ISSE interviews.
findings.remarks: Complete the Application Security and Development STIG checklist for each of the five containers, document the resulting settings in the baseline, record open items in stig-summary.yaml, and add a pipeline check for the settings that can be automated.

findings.title: The inventory was not reviewed or updated at release 1.5.1
findings.description: CM-8 as tailored requires the inventory to be reviewed and updated monthly and at every release. Release 1.5.1 reached the assessed environment on 2026-11-07; the inventory still lists the five containers at 1.5.0 and no review at that release is recorded. The monthly review of 2026-11-02 is on file and the inventory is otherwise complete and accurate. Evidence: the INV list, the review records, the ISSE interview.
findings.remarks: Review and update the inventory at each release as the SSP states, and record which release each environment runs, so the inventory matches the release deployed to production.

findings.title: The contingency plan is a draft: not reviewed or approved by the PM, not distributed, not under review
findings.description: CP-2 as tailored requires the contingency plan to be reviewed and approved by the PM, distributed to the on-call engineers, the ISSO, the ISSM, EMIS and the CSSP, reviewed annually and its changes communicated to them. The version 1.0 draft covers the content the control requires, but has no review or approval, has gone to nobody outside the program repository, and no review or change communication has happened. Evidence: ART-CP, the repository, the ISSE interview; the S-6 approval sets a PM approval date of 2026-12-15.
findings.remarks: Have the PM review and approve the plan by 2026-12-15, distribute it to the named personnel and to EMIS and the CSSP, and record the annual review date.

findings.title: Regional failover has never been tested and no tabletop exercise has been held
findings.description: CP-4 as tailored requires the contingency plan to be tested annually with a tabletop exercise, a database restore test and a regional failover test. Only the database restore has been tested (DT-2, re-performed by the assessor on 2026-12-02, within objective). The regional failover of the cluster, on which recovery from a regional outage depends, and the tabletop exercise have never been held; both are planned for 2027-02, after the planned deployment of 2027-02-01. Evidence: test records, the restore re-performance, the ISSE interview, conops limitation 4.
findings.remarks: Hold the tabletop and the regional failover test before production use if the schedule allows, otherwise as early in 2027-02 as possible, review the results and record corrective actions in the plan and the POA&M.

findings.title: Two break-glass console accounts authenticate with FIDO2 keys instead of CAC, and the deviation is not accepted
findings.description: IA-2 requires organizational users to be uniquely identified and authenticated, which DoD meets with CAC (PKI). The two break-glass cloud console accounts use FIDO2 hardware keys because the console cannot federate when the identity broker is down; each use is tied to a person only through the two-person seal log and the alert, not by the credential. The keys are sealed and unused; the deviation has not been recorded or accepted by the AO. Evidence: the account list, the seal log, the ISSO interview, conops limitation 5.
findings.remarks: Record the deviation with its compensating measures (sealed keys, two-person opening, alerting, post-use review) for the AO's acceptance, and review each break-glass use against the seal log within one working day.

findings.title: The local break-glass database role's password complexity falls short of the PostgreSQL STIG (STG-002, CAT II)
findings.description: IA-5 requires authenticators to have sufficient strength of mechanism for their intended use. The password of the local break-glass database role on INV-010 does not meet the PostgreSQL STIG complexity rule (STG-002, CAT II) on the 2026-10-22 scan and on the SCA's scan of release 1.5.1 on 2026-11-23. The password is sealed, changed within 180 days and its role unused. The fix is in release 1.5.2 (2026-12-10), not yet in pre-production. Evidence: both scans, stig-summary.yaml, the ISSO and ISSE interviews.
findings.remarks: Deploy release 1.5.2 with the database password policy the STIG requires, reset the break-glass password under it, rescan and close STG-002.
